paragraphs: In Birmingham, the council's fostering service is run by Birmingham Children's Trust, which looks after approximately 1,950 children in care. When a child in the city needs a foster home, the Trust first checks whether one of its own carers is available, and the independent fostering agencies listed below also care for Birmingham children.

The Trust wants carers from every background who reflect the diversity of the city. It says homes are most needed for children over 10 and teenagers, for brothers and sisters who need to stay together, for children with additional needs such as physical or learning disabilities, and for unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, who are usually teenage boys and may speak very little English. Professional experience with children is welcome but not required, and carers who already foster for another agency or council can apply to transfer.

Trust carers are given their own fostering social worker, a mentor who is an experienced foster carer, and training. The Trust says becoming a carer takes about six months, including training and assessment.

Agencies set their own fees and support packages, so it is worth speaking to the Trust and to two or three of the agencies on this page, and asking each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you decide.
